_comment: Project-level Claude Code settings for the GPU simulator: an event-driven Rust simulator with silicon-label validation; legacy non-root guard logic is historical only. Three hook groups support the unified knowledge base (353 non-index content cards plus two physical index/router files; `_template.md` is excluded; 355 generated manifest rows (14 subcorpora plus the two index/router files)) and local reference sources. (1) UserPromptSubmit runs scripts/kb/route_query.py — the merged router with 14 subcorpora and 10 routing destinations (9 active plus one retained historical measurement mapping) — against the SQLite FTS5 manifest (.claude/kb_manifest.sqlite, which must be rebuilt with `python3 scripts/kb/build_manifest.py` before ranked routing), then injects candidate cards and a skill pointer. It falls through to .claude/hooks/kb_reminder.sh when the manifest is missing or returns no match. (2) Stop runs scripts/kb/check_kb_usage.py in warning mode, appends to .claude/metrics/kb_usage.jsonl, and reminds when a KB-relevant prompt was answered without consulting .claude/knowledge/ or references/. The filesystem has 11 task-shaped Skills under .claude/skills/, including retained historical/scoped references; the router vocabulary is smaller. A historical path snapshot recorded 299/300 cited references resolving; revalidate before treating that as current. See docs/knowledge-routing.md. (3) SessionStart injects the binding 10-subagent concurrency ceiling so future sessions resume interrupted work and queue excess rather than fan out. Current policy comes from root CLAUDE.md, active schemas, runbooks, and ADRs. Personal overrides go in .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored).

hooks.command: printf '%s\n' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"Binding orchestration rule: never run more than 10 subagents concurrently. Count known live subagents before spawning; resume interrupted agents rather than duplicating them; serialize and queue all work beyond the 10-agent ceiling."}}'
